note: Canonical, machine-checkable requirement catalog for OAAF conformance. This file is the traceability spine (O6A). It is NOT the v1 conformance suite; O6H owns the v1 freeze. Statements are observable behaviors, not implementation algorithms. `keyword` uses BCP 14 (RFC 2119/8174). `source` cites the standard/RFC/ADR a requirement derives from — never a reference-implementation file.

requirements.statement: Verification MUST require an explicit trust-anchor set. Its absence is a configuration error, never a permissive default, and there MUST NOT be a mode that returns an authorization decision without one.
The root token MUST be verified against a configured trust anchor, not against its own cnf.jwk. A self-signed root that matches no anchor MUST be rejected.
Every token's signature MUST be cryptographically verified before any authority it asserts is used; an invalid signature on any chain member MUST deny.
An unsecured token (alg "none") MUST NOT be accepted, and a token MUST be verified only under a signature algorithm the pinned AAT profile permits; algorithm substitution MUST be rejected.
A derived token's iss MUST equal the JWK Thumbprint URI of its parent's verified cnf.jwk; a mismatch MUST deny.
A cnf.jwk MUST NOT contain private key material; a confirmation key carrying a private component MUST be rejected.
The proof-of-possession argument binding MUST be computed over the RFC 8785 (JCS) canonicalization of the argument map, so independent implementations bind identical bytes.
The chain MUST be verified in root-to-leaf order with each member linked to its parent; a reordered or relinked chain MUST deny.
An empty chain MUST deny.
A derived token's par_hash MUST match its parent, and a root token MUST NOT carry par_hash; either violation MUST deny.
A derived token MUST NOT raise del_max_depth above its parent's value; the ceiling is monotonic down the chain.
A token whose delegation depth exceeds the effective ceiling MUST deny.
A verifier MUST reject a delegation that grants authority (a tool) absent from its parent. Authority may only narrow across a delegation, never widen.
A derived constraint on a tool MUST NOT expand the parent's constraint; a derived clause MUST admit only a subset of the parent's permitted invocations.
For a constrained tool under a closed-world key set, a derived token MUST name exactly the same argument keys as its parent; adding or dropping a key MUST deny.
An unrecognized constraint type, or a subsumption pair the profile does not permit, MUST deny (fail closed) rather than be treated as satisfied.
A constrained argument is required: a request that omits an argument the leaf authority constrains MUST deny.
A request whose argument value violates the leaf authority's constraint on that argument MUST deny.
A requested tool not permitted by the verified leaf authority MUST deny.
A request carrying an argument the leaf authority does not permit for the tool MUST deny.
A token that is expired at the evaluation instant MUST deny; expiry applies to every member of the chain.
A token that is not yet valid at the evaluation instant MUST deny.
A derived token's validity window MUST NOT exceed its parent's; a later expiry or an earlier issuance than the parent MUST deny.
Enforcement MUST verify proof of possession, binding the presentation to the verified leaf holder's key and to the exact requested argument map.
There MUST NOT be an option that disables proof-of-possession verification while still presenting the result as an authorization decision.
A proof of possession whose key does not correspond to the verified leaf holder, or that does not match the presented tool and arguments, MUST deny.
A chain-only inspection operation MAY exist, but it MUST NOT emit an authorization decision and MUST be documented as not constituting enforcement.
The canonical subject MUST be the leaf token's sub when it is a valid URI, and otherwise the leaf holder's JWK Thumbprint URI.
The holder identity (the cnf.jwk thumbprint) MUST remain distinct from, and available alongside, the canonical subject.
The decision MUST be DENY whenever verification fails for any reason. This is the umbrella fail-closed rule.
Unknown, malformed, or unverifiable required authority MUST NOT degrade into ALLOW.
An implementation that encounters an unrecognized spec or profile version MUST refuse the exchange rather than guess at its meaning.
Where the same authority material is accepted through more than one supported binding, the canonical authority decision MUST NOT change because of the transport.
A decision MUST be expressible as an outcome of ALLOW or DENY, and a DENY MUST carry at least one stable reason code.

For a check named by a normative reason code (see classification), a denial produced by that check MUST report that code. Finer or coarser diagnostic codes MAY additionally be used but MUST NOT replace the normative code for that check.
An explanation MUST NOT include key material, raw token bytes, signatures, proof-of-possession material, or argument values the caller did not already supply.
An implementation MAY provide additional diagnostic fields (locators, stage labels, human-readable messages) without breaking conformance. Human-readable message wording is not normative.
Core conformance MUST NOT depend on MCP, A2A, or any particular transport binding.
Core conformance MUST NOT require any particular identity provider (e.g. SPIFFE, WIMSE, OIDC).
Core conformance MUST NOT require any particular policy decision point or an OAAF-hosted authorization service.
Core conformance MUST NOT require an OAAF-hosted revocation or status service.
A conformant implementation MUST NOT be required to share a language, library, internal API, object model, source structure, or package name with any reference implementation.
When a status resolver is configured, every token in the chain MUST be checked for revocation.
If any chain member resolves to revoked, the decision MUST deny.
If any chain member resolves to unknown, the decision MUST deny (fail closed), unless the deployment has explicitly opted into a documented allow-unknown mode that MUST NOT be the default.
A revoked ancestor MUST invalidate every chain that contains it, even when the leaf itself is active.
A resolver backed by a bounded-freshness status artifact MUST treat an artifact past its freshness as unknown, not as its last-known contents.
Absent a configured resolver, verification MUST remain expiry-only and fully offline; status checking MUST NOT be silently assumed.
When an identity-binding verifier is configured and reports mismatch for the subject and holder, the decision MUST deny.
When a required identity binding is unavailable, the decision MUST deny (fail closed), unless the deployment has opted into a documented weaker mode.
Absent a configured verifier, the authority issuer's signed sub assertion is trusted; identity binding MUST NOT be silently assumed to have been externally verified.
An OIDC subject MUST be composed with its issuer into a collision-safe URI; a bare sub MUST NOT be used alone across issuers.
A syntactically valid identity URI MUST NOT by itself be treated as cross-domain trust; trust anchors and the binding verifier remain the arbiters.
OAAF authority MUST be enforced as a precondition before the COAZ AuthZEN request is constructed; on any OAAF denial the PEP MUST refuse immediately and MUST NOT proceed to the PDP.
OAAF MUST NOT redefine COAZ/MCP request semantics (subject, action, resource); it contributes only an additional precondition and an optional context member.
On success the PEP MAY add a context.oaaf member carrying the canonical authority context.
A skill gated by OAAF MUST declare the OAAF extension required; if the extension was not activated, the agent MUST refuse the operation and MUST NOT perform it.
Before any consequential operation on a gated skill, the agent MUST verify OAAF authority; a request lacking verifiable authority material MUST deny.
When the proof of possession carries an aat_aud, it MUST equal the recipient agent's stable A2A identity; a mismatch MUST deny.
The proof-of-possession holder and the AAT leaf holder MUST correspond. The A2A-authenticated caller identity and the AAT holder MAY differ unless the deployment requires them equal.

OAAF conveys verified authority facts to the policy decision point; it MUST NOT make the organization's policy decision. OAAF decides whether delegated authority is valid; the PDP decides whether policy permits the action.
The authority context MUST be derived only from a verified authority; its authorityVerified marker states OAAF's authority decision, not that the action is permitted.
The PDP profile MUST NOT require a particular policy engine; AuthZEN context is the canonical carrier and other engines are documented adapters.
The authority context MUST carry names, never values, matching the privacy rule of the explanation.
